title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Conflicting Obligation Capacity Reservation and Reliance Arbitration Extension

parent_binding.extension_rule: v1.4 adds future commit capacity reservation and deterministic conflict handling for multiple host obligations

core_problem: A host with multiple faces can create overcommitment even when every individual face is sincere. Host-global future capacity must therefore be reserved and checked atomically before admitting new obligations.

new_primitives.CAPACITY_RESOURCE_ID: Stable identifier for a scarce future execution resource such as one body, tool channel, exclusive authority scope, time window or consumable budget.
new_primitives.RESERVATION_ID: Identifier linking one obligation to reserved future capacity.
new_primitives.RESERVED_WINDOW: Time or causal interval in which the obligation expects access to a resource.
new_primitives.CAPACITY_AMOUNT: Quantity or exclusivity requirement for the resource.
new_primitives.CONFLICT_SET: Set of obligations or candidates that cannot all be performed under the currently known world model.
new_primitives.RELIANCE_WEIGHT_METADATA: Recorded external dependence relevant to repairability and urgency; not a moral worth score for the counterparty.
new_primitives.REPAIR_OBLIGATION: Secondary obligation created when an admitted commitment cannot be fulfilled and repair remains possible.
new_primitives.FEASIBILITY_EPOCH: Versioned world-model state under which compatibility was last evaluated.

atomic_obligation_admission.atomicity_rule: Obligation commit and capacity reservation must succeed or fail as one logical transaction.
failure_modes_prevented: two faces concurrently reserve the same exclusive body slot
promise is committed but reservation write fails
reservation exists without a corresponding active obligation
face-local planner ignores commitments created by another face

known_conflict_rule.condition: Current world model shows that existing and proposed obligations cannot both be performed within the reserved capacity.
known_conflict_rule.important_boundary: Sincerity, face novelty and internal majority do not override physical capacity.

latent_conflict_rule.condition: Obligations were compatible at admission but a later world observation makes joint performance impossible.
effects: notify affected counterparties when a communication channel exists
search for delegation or alternate performance consistent with consent and authority
arbitrate remaining incompatibility using auditable metadata
create repair obligation for any valid commitment left unperformed
latent_conflict_rule.forbidden: Retroactively rewrite an honest prior obligation as if it had never been admitted.

repair_protocol.trigger: A valid obligation remains unperformed after conflict arbitration.
steps: preserve original promise and conflict provenance
offer feasible mitigation or replacement performance
record counterparty release or revision separately if granted
retain breach/repair history even after eventual fulfillment

must_reconstruct: which reservations existed before each obligation commit
whether a conflict was knowable at that exact feasibility epoch
which world observation later created a latent conflict
which arbitration metadata selected the performed obligation
which repair obligation was created for the unperformed commitment
tamper_tests: change safety metadata to alter priority
mark capacity released without discharge receipt
split same physical body into fake face-local resource ids

ai_agent_bridge.rule: Multiple planners, personas or model contexts controlling shared actuators need a single reservation authority at the host boundary.
ai_agent_bridge.boundary: This does not imply autonomous legal personhood; it specifies technical accountability for persistent agent-like systems.

en: A promise reserves future causal capacity.
Many sincere faces still share one body, one clock and one external world.
Known overcommitment is an admission failure, not a future face's problem to hide.
When reality changes after honest commitments, preserve both histories, recompute feasibility and repair what cannot be performed.
Commit priority must be replayable from obligation metadata, not from identity preference.
